title: What Prahlada learned
hookLine: a demon king asks his son what school taught him, and the week's sounds gathered into three ways to love God
carry: hearing, singing, remembering: the first ways to love god
tomorrow: why would Nani gasp when you step over a notebook?

lines: WHAT DID YOU LEARN AT SCHOOL?
A DEMON KING ASKS HIS SON.
cards: A parent picks a kid up and asks the oldest question: so, what did you learn at school? This parent is Hiranyakashipu, king of the demons, who hates Vishnu above everything.
He takes his little son Prahlada on his lap and asks: of all you've learned, what's the best? Prahlada answers, sweetly, in front of everyone. And the room goes cold.

teach.b: Here's what he says, in the Bhagavata Purana. The best learning is to love Vishnu in nine ways. Hearing about him.
Singing about him. Remembering him. Serving his feet.
Worshipping him. Bowing to him. Being his servant.
Being his friend. And offering him everything you are. The king is furious and blames the teachers, who swear they taught no such thing.

teach.h: HEARD FROM NARADA, IN THE WOMB.
teach.b: Later Prahlada tells his classmates where it came from: he heard the sage Narada teaching while he was still in his mother's womb.
Hindus call this list navadha bhakti, the nine ways of devotion, and notice where it starts: with the ears and the voice. That's this week.
Hearing: Shiva's drum and the word held sacred, shabda brahman, and Hanuman, who chose to spend forever listening to Rama's story. Singing: Tyagaraja, giving his voice to Rama instead of the king.
Remembering: the name, said with care or said backwards, Valmiki's mara, mara, and Ajamila calling his son. And under all of it, prana, the breath every word rides on.
The nine ways run on into service, worship and friendship. But the door Prahlada names first is the one this week walked through.

how: Hindus practice the first ways of devotion every day: listening to katha and bhajans, singing kirtan, and repeating a name of God in japa; Prahlada's list of nine is often taught to children.

o: the sounds of devotion: heard, sung and remembered
the sounds of a king's court at war

games.q: the boy and the nine ways — tap the pairs.
p: the boy who named nine ways to love God
the demon king who hated Vishnu

s: Prahlada learned the nine ways from his school teachers
the teachers denied it; he said he heard Narada while still in the womb.
hearing about God comes first in Prahlada's list
shravana, then kirtana, singing, then smarana, remembering.
navadha bhakti says only temple worship counts as devotion
worship is one of nine; hearing, singing and remembering count too.

games.q: Sam asks, 'does it count as praying if your Nani plays bhajans all day while she cooks?' what's the best answer?
o: yes: hearing and singing about God are two of Prahlada's nine ways.
no: it only counts in front of the shrine.
only if she understands every word.
games.why: Prahlada names hearing and singing as devotion, alongside worship and the rest. Nani's kitchen counts.

practice: Choose one of the three. Hear: listen to one bhajan or chant you love, start to finish. Sing: hum one line of it.
Remember: say one name of God slowly, three times. If you don't pray, choose a sound that matters to you and give it one full minute of attention. Then rest with the breath.

wordCard.voice: The sounds: this week, heard, sung and remembered, the first three of Prahlada's nine ways.

orig.note: Sanskrit: navadhā bhakti, devotion in nine ways, from Prahlada's answer in the Bhagavata Purana.

carryVoice: The week's line: hearing, singing, remembering, the first ways to love God. That's the week.

sources.ref: Bhagavata Purana 7.5.22–28 (Prahlada's answer: hearing, singing, remembering, serving, worship, bowing, service, friendship, self-offering; his teachers deny teaching it)
Bhagavata Purana 7.7.14–16 (Prahlada heard Narada's teaching in his mother's womb)
